outcome: maternal complications (postpartum hemorrhage, puerperal pyrexia, sepsis, maternal death, wound gaping, pelvic abscess)
cohort: 120 pregnant individuals referred to a tertiary care center in Gujarat, India with a gestational age greater than 24 weeks, excluding gynecological referrals and postpartum cases.
finding: Referred obstetric cases presented diverse delivery modes (vaginal delivery 30.83%, LSCS 47.67%, VBAC 3.33%, hysterectomy 2.50%), maternal complications (postpartum hemorrhage 5%, puerperal pyrexia 9.17%, sepsis 1.67%, maternal death 1.67%, wound gaping 1.67%, pelvic abscess 1.67%), and neonatal outcomes (NICU admission 3.33%, IUD 2.50%).
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery occurred in 30.83% of participants, lower segment cesarean section in 47.67%, vaginal birth after cesarean in 3.33%, and hysterectomy in 2.50%.
